```text
of your night will be composed of NREM sleep, which will get progres-
sively deeper as the night continues. When we enter deep sleep, our brain
waves get long and slow, and our blood pressure drops while our muscles
relax. Once we shift from NREM to REM sleep, our brains become active
and dreaming occurs. If you are sleeping well, you’ll cycle between the
two types of sleep several times per night until it’s time to get up.
    What’s particularly interesting is that learning is consolidated during
sleep. For this reason, it’s helpful to take a nap or go to sleep right after
studying new material. We now have good data to show that poor quality,
fragmented sleep impacts memory negatively.
    Insomnia (which is trouble falling asleep or staying asleep for the entire
night) is a common problem for many poker players. It can be exacerbated
if you have to travel across time zones for events. It is also associated with
stress, depression, anxiety, alcohol consumption, and/or poor diet.
    Insomnia may not seem like a problem, but over time it can lead to
brain shrinkage. You can experience symptoms that include memory
lapses, irritability, and difficulty concentrating. If you have insomnia, the
best thing to do is consult your physician to get a physical and more in-
formation about what to do. You can also consult the website for the Na-
tional Sleep Foundation for more information.
    The second biggest sleep issue that affects the general population is
sleep apnea. This disorder is characterized by dropping oxygen levels dur-
ing sleep, because you stop breathing. Sleep studies show that people
with this condition can stop breathing for as long as 60 seconds at a time,
many times an hour, each night. Such lapses starve your brain of oxygen.
If you have sleep apnea, you’ll tend to be tired even after a full night’s
sleep, and you’ll have trouble with memory, focus, and problem solving.
    How to know if you have sleep apnea? A group of researchers at the
University of Toronto devised a mnemonic device to help people assess
their risk of apnea called the STOP BANG. If you answer yes to three or
more, you are at high risk and should get checked out by your doctor. The
only way to know for sure is to get a sleep study done at the direction of
your physician.
```

```text
   Studies of patients with sleep apnea show that their brain waves are
extremely sluggish. Instead of displaying the alert and focused alpha
waves during the day, they show a lot of slow theta waves. If you have
this problem, focusing at the poker table is going to be very difficult, if
not impossible. The good news is that all sleep issues have treatments
that are readily available.
   If you have the good fortune not to have a sleep problem, you can still
reap the benefits of being more focused and attentive during sessions if
you pay attention to getting enough sleep. Your game will thank you, and
so will your brain.
```

```text
   If you think you might suffer from depression, seek out the advice of a
qualified mental health professional or your physician. Depression can have
underlying medical causes (like thyroid problems or sleep apnea), which can
be treated. Even if you don’t experience depression, we know that stress is
associated with slower thinking and increased forgetfulness. These prob-
lems are likely due to all the brain changes that occur when you are under
stress. Here are just some of the negative brain changes that happen in a
stressed brain:

   ♠ The high levels of cortisol released when we are stressed are
       associated with poor memory.
   ♠ Chronic stress causes at least some nerve cells in the hippocampus
       and the prefrontal cortex to shrink.
   ♠ Chronic stress also causes nerve cells in the hippocampus to lose
       connections with one another.
   ♠ Stress lowers brain-derived neurotrophic factor levels.
   ♠ Stress damages the prefrontal cortex and impairs decision making
       and impulse control.
   ♠ Chronic stress can increase the size of your amygdala, which can
       lead to anxiety, fear, and aggression.
   ♠ Stress is associated with non-optimal brain waves.
```

```text
                    Enhance Your Brain’s Performance: Brain Boosters

    The good news is that even if you have been experiencing a good bit of
stress, there are steps you can take to minimize the damage. In addition,
the damage caused by stress and even depression is completely reversi-
ble, if you take steps to treat the underlying problem.
    As you can see, stress can have many profound negative effects on
your brain. It can be difficult to remove stress, but we can learn to handle
it more effectively. You can practice regular meditation, yoga, or tai chi.
All of these have been shown to reduce stress. If you are feeling acute
stress, like when you have just taken a bad beat, consider stepping away
from the table to do some power breathing, as described below.

Power Breathing
Breathe in through your nose to a slow count of four. Make sure that you
breathe very deeply such that your belly pushes out. Exhale out of your
mouth for a count of eight. Repeat this breathing pattern for at least one
minute. The trick is to make sure that your exhale lasts twice as long as
your inhale because, contrary to what most people think, stress relief
comes on the exhalation and not on the inhalation.
    Power breathing is very effective for soothing your brain, because it
increases your heart rate variability; your heart rate increases a bit during
inhalation and decreases a bit during exhalation. The more variability there
is between your heart beats, the better. When you breathe deeply like
this, you also shift your body out of the fight or flight pattern into what is
known as the calm and connect mode. Basically, you are going from sym-
pathetic stimulation (an amped up mode to prepare you for fight or flight)
to parasympathetic stimulation, which calms and relaxes your entire
nervous system. You’ll immediately notice that your heart rate decreases
and that you feel more calm and clear.

Summary
This chapter and the previous one have shown that the brain is an infi-
nitely complex system that contains a ton of moving parts. To keep your
mind in tip top condition there are a number of strategies you can try.
```

```text
Peak Poker Performance

Here are a few that I recommend most strongly if you are trying to spe-
cifically enhance your A game:

   ♠ Work on attention issues. Exercise and fish oil supplements have
       shown that they are powerful weapons in the fight to improve
       attention. Check with your doctor before adding anything new to
       your routine. Mindfulness meditation is also very helpful for
       attention problems; there is instruction on meditation in Chapter 7.
   ♠ Build brain healthy habits. Eating well, sleeping well, exercising, and
       meditating form the base of a peak performance pyramid. We
       have included chapters in this book on developing success habits
       and systems. Your mission should be to optimize these areas as
       much as possible because they are critical to your brain health and
       your long-term success as a poker player.
   ♠ Work on your emotional fitness. Having more positive emotions
       than negative ones each day is very important to your mental
       health. Learn to reduce stress. Practice mindfulness and power
       breathe regularly. Every little bit helps.
   ♠ Treat any medical conditions. Whether it is poor sleep, high blood
       pressure, or high cholesterol, if your body is not functioning well,
       your brain cannot perform at its highest level. The longer you have
       these problems, the more damage that is done to your brain. There
       are effective treatments for all these problems, and solving them
       may be just what you need to give your game an extra boost.

Chapter Highlights
   ♠ You have the ability to affect change and increase growth in your
       brain at any age.
   ♠ Exercise increases brain-derived neurotrophic factor, the Miracle-
       Gro for your brain.
```

```text
Jonathan’s Comments
Brain Booster #1: Exercise
About eight years ago when I realized I was out of shape, I decided to get
in the gym and start working out. I am confident that my ability to think
clearly went through the roof after I started my exercise routine. Prior to
getting in the gym I was effectively auto-piloting at a high enough level
to succeed. Afterwards, I become much more aware while playing poker,
which allowed me to make more plays to take advantage of my oppo-
nents’ mistakes.

walk for one minute for about 20 minutes total. I would mix it up from
time to time, perhaps sprinting two minutes and walking two minutes.
Eventually I decided to push myself too hard, which came in the form of
trying to run a five minute mile. I was able to run a mile in about five and a
half minutes but then I hurt my right foot. I went to the doctor and he es-
```

```text
Peak Poker Performance

quickly wearing away. Bad beat! I now spend my cardio time in the gym,
on either the elliptical trainer or the bicycle, again sticking with primarily
high-intensity interval training. I find it marginally enjoyable and am al-
ways dead tired after finishing. It is great.

Brain Booster #2: Diet
In the past, I ate incredibly poorly. My diet consisted entirely of fast food,
microwavable meals, and soda. I eventually figured out that these foods
are unhealthy. Of course, I weighed 40 pounds more then than I do now. I
now consume primarily grilled meats, vegetables, green tea, and water.
While I occasionally allow myself to splurge on some wine or a dessert,
those occasions are relatively rare. I can confidently say that I feel much
better now than I ever did in the past. I usually feel fine after every meal,
whereas in the past I would feel nauseous. To look better, feel better, and
increase your brain’s potential, eating right will put you on the right path.

Brain Booster #3: Mindfulness Meditation
When Positive Poker came out, I was just getting into meditation. Now, I
meditate for at least some time almost every day. I tend to either sit or
lay down and clear my mind of all the irrelevant things that constantly pop
into my consciousness. It is amazing how wild my brain is! Even spending
10 minutes meditating each morning before I start my day sets me up to
be much more productive than when I don’t.
   I have also found that brief meditation sessions at the poker table al-
low me to stay completely off tilt. When something happens that bothers
me in the least bit, I will take a few deep breaths, forget about the game
for a minute, recognize I am thankful for the opportunity at hand, and
then return to the game calm and refreshed. Playing poker is quite enjoy-
able when you never get tilted.
```

```text
eight hours of sleep, I am incredibly cranky. One time when I went to Italy

     I figure out my sleep schedule before I go and play poker. For example,
if I am going to Spain to play on the European Poker Tour, I start adjusting
my sleep about an hour each day until I am waking up at about 10am
Spanish time. This allows me not to have to worry about quickly adjusting
to the local time zone. I also make a point of not staying out too late. I am
not the stereotypical poker player who plays poker until 6am then sleeps
until 2pm. Given I play tournaments that typically start at noon, and I
realize maximizing my equity in those is my main priority, I forego poten-
tially profitable late night poker games and parties.
     It is amazing to me how many poker players have not been on a proper
sleep schedule for years. Many elect to play whenever the games are
good, which usually results in abnormal sleeping patterns. Players who
sleep poorly are generally crabby and unhappy. If they spent a bit less
time at the poker table and a little more time asleep, I think they would
see a drastic increase in their level of happiness. It is important to recog-
nize that feeling great is often more important than playing an additional
hour of poker each day.

my mind before each session. If anything goes the least bit poorly at the
table, I take a few deep breaths and remain stoic. This allows me to con-
stantly play my best.
```
